claims.text: Coatings deposited from 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock have inadequate thickness for the required bond-coat performance.
Increasing the FeCoNiCrAl feedstock particle-size range from 15–45 μm to approximately 45–75 μm will increase coating thickness.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will enhance deposition efficiency relative to the 15–45 μm feedstock.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will preserve coating integrity relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The 45–75 μm feedstock will limit in-flight oxidation.
Larger feedstock particles have a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio.
Larger feedstock particles have greater momentum under the proposed spray conditions.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger particles reduces in-flight oxidation.
The increased momentum of larger particles improves deposition efficiency.
Reduced oxidation and enhanced impact kinetic energy promote better particle melting and bonding.
Improved particle melting and bonding produce thicker deposits without compromising microstructural integrity or increasing as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective under standard atmospheric plasma-spray conditions with controlled oxygen levels and subsequent high-temperature oxidative service.
The intervention is expected to remain effective for feedstock particle sizes up to about 75 μm.
Particle sizes exceeding about 75 μm may hinder proper particle melting and deposition quality.
